transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because I’m not really sleeping. I’ll lie there for hours… if it’s raining, or I start thinking about the bluff giving way, I just can’t shut it off. And when I do fall asleep, I wake up sweating from dreams. Then I go into the call center feeling like I didn’t sleep at all.
Have you been having intrusive thoughts or flashbacks about a specific stressful or traumatic event?

Yeah… I guess so. Stuff will just pop into my head, like the sound of rocks sliding, or my leg stuck under me. For a second it’s like I’m not at my desk with the headset on anymore… I’m back on that trail.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities because they remind you of what happened on the trail?
Yeah… I don’t go near those coast trails anymore. And when my old hiking friends text, I usually just ignore it. Even talking about going back out there makes my chest get tight.
Do you find yourself being easily startled or feeling on edge a lot, like you’re always watching for danger?
I’m not really sure. I mean… I guess I notice noises more sometimes, but I don’t know if I’d say I’m always watching for danger.
Do you often feel like you’re constantly on guard, even in safe places, as if you’re always expecting something bad to happen?

Yeah… kind of. I don’t really relax much. I keep thinking I was stupid for going out there alone, and if I’m not paying attention, something bad could happen again… even when I know I’m probably fine.
Have you been having nightmares or disturbing dreams about what happened on the trail?

Yeah… I do. Not every single night, but enough. I’ll finally fall asleep and then wake up sweating from dreams about the bluff, or the trail giving way. Then I go into work feeling like I didn’t sleep at all.
